files.role: Public encoded-file concatenation and validated data-file-part API. Owns local compatibility, Blob descriptor/lease gates, page-buffer relocation, exact-version structural hooks and output factory/abort sequencing. Dataset authority, transaction/retry, fallback implementation and source-object immutability are caller boundaries.
ranges: SPDX and module contract: copy complete encoded files, owning compatibility and metadata relocation while callers own Dataset grouping, transactions and fallback. Imports provide ordered maps/sets, descriptor queues, Arrow inspection, Blob schema handling, decoder metadata, FileScheduler/ObjectWriter, protobuf Any serialization, version dispatch and writer options. No process configuration, global mutable state, unsafe block or explicit task spawn is introduced.

Public BlobTargetId is a private-field Arc<str> newtype with Clone/Debug/value equality. new accepts Into<Arc<str>> without nonempty/namespace validation; as_str borrows its contents. It is caller-defined runtime equality only, with no persistence, storage authority, recovery or Dataset identity guarantee.

Public Clone EncodedFileInput privately owns a clonable FileScheduler and optional expected u64 row count. new defaults the expectation to None; with_expected_num_rows consumes self and stores any value, including zero. path borrows the scheduler reader path; private scheduler clones the handle. Neither construction nor setting the expectation performs IO or validates immutability.

Public Clone DataFilePart owns EncodedFileInput, Arc cached metadata, Arc normalized schema, optional half-open Blob lease and optional BlobTargetId. Documentation says complete independently readable runtime file, not persisted Manifest fragment/checkpoint. Caller owns storage and Blob association; caller order is physical row order. Example awaits open with no lease/target and prints rows. Custom Debug exposes path, exact version, footer row count, lease and target, omitting complete schema/metadata.

DataFilePart::open first validates any supplied Blob range before IO, then reads all metadata, normalizes anonymous Blob descriptor children and checks optional expected rows against footer count. A mismatch is InvalidInput naming path, actual and expected, before Blob checks. Stored scheduler/metadata have no local ETag/content-hash binding or later immutability recheck.

Open rejects any normalized schema field with is_blob&&!is_blob_v2 as NotSupported. It projects descriptor form and delegates exact-version complete-column/uniform-length validation; every delegated error is wrapped as CorruptFile with the input path and incomplete metadata context. Returned normalized length must equal footer rows, otherwise CorruptFile. This validates encoded metadata, not all non-Blob data values.

If any schema field is Blob v2, open awaits descriptor validation before checking that target ID is Some. Thus missing target may be reported only after descriptor IO or a descriptor error. A Blob schema needs a target even if every descriptor is null/empty/external; a lease is required by managed values, not by schema alone. Successful open retains all inputs/Arcs/options unchanged; public num_rows returns metadata footer count.

descriptor_projection_schema clones Schema and applies BlobHandling::BlobsDescriptions.unload_if_needed to each root, preserving the cloned outer schema. descriptor_child_matches requires id=-1,parent_id=-1,matching name/logical type and no children. It does not compare nullability, metadata, dictionary, encoding or other Field attributes.

attach_blob_descriptor_children traverses fields in preorder. A childless is_blob field consumes the next queued child vector if present; when the queue is empty it remains childless. Other fields recurse. Matching is positional, not by a persisted parent ID, and there is no Result or leftover/missing-queue check.

normalize_blob_footer_schema counts every childless is_blob field, not only v2. With none it returns a schema clone. Otherwise it scans only top-level fields for contiguous runs matching the five descriptor children from BLOB_V2_DESC_LANCE_FIELD, drains up to the missing count into a queue, and attaches those runs to missing Blob parents in preorder. Draining holds the current index; unmatched roots advance it. Partial reconstruction silently returns, and child attribute mismatches outside the narrow matcher do not prevent reassociation. This reads the existing anonymous-ID footer representation without writing a new format.

validate_blob_id_range accepts None; Some requires start>=1 and start<end. InvalidInput includes start..end. The u32 half-open endpoint means a lease cannot contain u32::MAX. This function validates declared range shape only, without reserving IDs or examining descriptors.

Descriptor validation builds a descriptor-projected schema, collects Blob v2 field IDs and BTreeSet uniqueness. Duplicate IDs or a negative minimum produce CorruptFile. project_by_ids(...,true) keeps structural context. Exact data_file_columns maps IDs to physical columns; zipped pairs with either negative value are dropped and remaining u32 pairs collect into BTreeMap, with later duplicate keys replacing earlier ones. Exact reader_projection_from_field_ids may fail.

Descriptor validator reopens FileReader with selected projection, default DecoderPlugins/options and no cache; this is another metadata open after DataFilePart::open read_all_metadata. It streams RangeFull with8192 row batches,readahead4,no filter. Each batch allocates an all-true selection vector and recursively validates zipped Arrow fields/arrays. It decodes descriptor arrays rather than Blob payload content and does not collect the whole stream.

validate_blob_field handles Arrow field.is_blob first, assuming a Struct array and named primitive kind(UInt8),position/size(UInt64),blob_id(UInt32) columns. Missing names are CorruptFile; AsArray type mismatches can panic. It enumerates the supplied selection and skips unselected or null descriptor rows. No independent selection-length or child-validity check exists here; schema/Arrow construction are trusted. blob_uri is not fetched or validated.

BlobKind conversion can reject unknown byte kinds. Inline with size>0 is InvalidInput; zero-size Inline is accepted without position/ID checks. Packed/Dedicated require Some lease and ID membership; Dedicated additionally requires position0 or CorruptFile. Packed offsets/sizes and managed payload existence/length are not checked, and repeated IDs within a lease are allowed. External passes without URI/base/offset/size validation. Return after handling a Blob field, without recursively validating descriptor children as ordinary fields.

For ordinary Struct, intersect selected rows with parent validity, allocate a child-selection Vec<bool> and recurse through zipped children/columns. Invalid parent rows suppress checks of otherwise populated descendants. There is no explicit child-count equality check in this helper.

For List(i32), allocate false flags for the complete child value array; each selected valid parent marks its offset interval true, then recurse into the values. Offset casts/range slicing trust valid Arrow invariants and can panic on inconsistent arrays or selection lengths. Null/unselected parent items remain unvalidated.

LargeList repeats List propagation with i64 offsets cast to usize. All other Arrow data types take an empty branch, including FixedSizeList/Map/ListView-style containers at this local boundary. The function returns Ok after recursive validation; it has no direct tests in this file for container nulls or those unhandled shapes.

Public Clone/Debug FileConcatTarget exposes exact ConcreteFileVersion and Arc<Schema>, with private optional Blob target. new stores version/schema and None without validation; with_blob_target_id consumes self and sets Some. Release aliases must already be resolved; the type itself does not enforce target/source storage separation.

Public FileConcatOptions exposes read_batch_bytes:usize and writer_options:FileWriterOptions. Default threshold is16*1024*1024 bytes plus writer defaults. Despite the maximum wording, batching never splits one page, so a single oversized page can exceed the threshold. Zero is rejected only in concat_prepared, after entrypoint metadata reads.

Public Copy/Clone/Debug/Eq FileConcatOutput contains exact version,u64 total physical rows,u64 object size. Written uses writer summary; Reused uses loaded input metadata file_size_bytes. No path, Dataset fragment ID or Blob ID lease is returned.

Public FileConcatReason starts with LegacyVersion, VersionMismatch(input_index,actual,expected), SchemaMismatch(input_index), ColumnLayoutMismatch(input_index,optional physical column) and ColumnEncodingMismatch(input_index,column_index). These are structured compatibility outcomes, not necessarily errors; indices are zero-based.

Remaining compatibility variants are ColumnBuffers(input/column/count), ExtraGlobalBuffers(input/count including schema) and BlobColumns. Column/global buffers lack relocation support at this layer. BlobColumns applies to the ordinary concat target schema; the validated-part path explicitly permits Blob schemas.

Display formats legacy/version/schema/layout/encoding reasons. Layout None denotes different physical-column count, Some identifies a physical column. Version display uses ConcreteFileVersion Display; messages do not include source paths here.

Display reports exact unsupported column/global buffer counts and a general Blob rejection string. It implements fmt::Display only; FileConcatReason is not declared an Error. These strings are used by higher-level callers to choose error/fallback presentation.

Public Eq FileConcatResult distinguishes Written(output), Reused(input index,output) and Unsupported(reason); Unsupported promises no output factory call. Private PreparedInput borrows input,metadata,schema for one attempt. encoded_column_encoding serializes ColumnInfo.encoding through protobuf Any into owned bytes; comparison is serialized column encoding equality, not page encoding equality.

check_compatibility first rejects any Blob in the ordinary target schema, then requires a first prepared input. It derives the baseline physical columns from the first input, descriptor-projects the target only for part mode, and serializes all baseline column encodings before checking input row/version/schema. It does not itself reject target V1; public ordinary dispatch handles legacy earlier.

Per-input check order is expected footer rows(InvalidInput), exact version(Unsupported VersionMismatch), complete Schema equality(Unsupported SchemaMismatch), exact external-metadata validation(CorruptFile wrapping any delegated error), then normalized/footer row equality(CorruptFile). No coercion, alias equivalence, column reordering or semantic encoding comparison is attempted.

After metadata validation, more than one global buffer gives Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers; schema buffer0 is regenerated. Different column count versus the first input gives ColumnLayoutMismatch(None), although prior schema/metadata checks may reject first. A zero-global buffer case has no local rejection here; valid readers normally require schema storage upstream.

Each physical column must have no column-level buffers, the same index as baseline and identical serialized column-level encoding. Error order is ColumnBuffers then index layout then encoding mismatch. Different page encodings/page counts are allowed if preceding validation succeeds. Returns None after every input; it never reads page payloads or validates their absolute ranges against EOF.

copy_page_buffers allocates output PageInfo capacity equal to page count and groups consecutive complete pages. For each page, checked offset+size rejects u64 range overflow and checked sum(size) rejects page byte-count overflow as contextual CorruptFile with path,input,column,page. There is no local offset+size<=file_size check; subsequent scheduler IO determines out-of-file behavior.

A page after the first in a batch is deferred when checked cumulative bytes overflow or exceed read_batch_bytes. The first page is always admitted, even oversized. The aggregate addition is then checked. Buffer counts include zero lengths but read ranges omit them; positive offset+size arithmetic is safe only because the earlier checked pass succeeded. Page boundaries/order are preserved, with no sorting/coalescing here.

One scheduler request at priority0 returns all positive-length ranges in the batch, or no IO occurs if none. Consume one returned Bytes per nonempty buffer; missing response or unequal byte length is contextual IO error, including overlong results under the short-read wording. Zero buffers consume no result but still call writer.write_external_buffer(empty). Each buffer is written sequentially and its new offset/size retained.

After writing all buffers of each page, clone its encoding, preserve num_rows and checked-add whole-input row_offset to priority. Priority overflow is InvalidInput after possible output writes. Extra returned buffers are rejected only after the batch writes. Retain relocated PageInfo for all pages; no page decoding, retry, checksum or rollback occurs in this helper.

concat_prepared is generic over a FnOnce async output factory. Reject zero read threshold, run compatibility, checked-sum footer row counts, and return Reused(0,metadata size) for exactly one ordinary input. This path never calls the factory or validates/uses writer_options. Part mode passes reuse_single_input=false and always creates output after checks, even for one part.

After all compatibility and total-row checks, await output factory and exact create_lazy_writer. Both calls are outside the write_result async block, so an error here does not invoke the explicit writer.abort branch below. Allocate one Vec<PageInfo> per first-input physical column and row_offset0. No metadata/page count memory budget or streaming footer builder exists here.

Traverse inputs in caller order and columns in metadata order, invoking exact copy_external_metadata_column with whether that output column already has pages. Its closure copies buffers and appends relocated pages. Checked row_offset advances once per input after all its columns. V2_0 dispatch may skip later structural header columns; V2_1/2/3 invoke every copy. This loop is sequential across files/columns and retains all output page metadata.

Finalize each output column through exact-version hook, then create ColumnInfo with baseline index/encoding, moved accumulated pages and an empty column-buffer vector. V2_0 structural header finalization reduces to one page with total rows/priority0; other current versions leave pages unchanged. Output page encodings can remain heterogeneous.

An empty external-buffer write aligns the upcoming schema descriptor. initialize_with_external_columns receives target schema clone, constructed columns and total rows; finish writes normal metadata/footer and shuts down. Success returns Written with exact target version and writer summary counts/size. Any error inside write_result awaits writer.abort then returns the original error; abort returns no Result here. There is no cancellation Drop guard, and cancellation before reaching the match does not execute this explicit abort.

Public concat_files documentation promises one metadata-read pass per input, pre-factory compatibility, no Arrow page decoding and regenerated offsets/priorities/structural metadata/footer. Doctest supplies a store.create async factory. Exact generic signature accepts borrowed target and ordered input slice, an owned FnOnce()->Future<Result<Box<dyn ObjectWriter>>> and owned options; no Send bound is imposed on that factory in this entrypoint.

concat_files rejects empty input before IO. try_join_all concurrently reads raw metadata for every input, retaining ordered results and propagating any read error. Only afterward, target V1 or any raw Legacy result returns Unsupported LegacyVersion, before expected-row/read-batch/ordinary Blob checks. Even a V1 target causes source metadata reads; invalid source may therefore return Err instead of Unsupported.

Finalize all current raw metadata through exact-version finish_metadata before borrowing it into PreparedInput; encountering Legacy here is an Internal defensive error after the earlier guard. Prepared schema is the actual file_schema, with no Blob normalization on ordinary path. Invoke concat_prepared with Blob disabled and single-input reuse enabled. Payload copying happens later and assumes caller-preserved immutable inputs.

Public concat_data_file_parts accepts validated DataFilePart slice with the same generic factory contract. It rejects empty parts, then compares every part optional BlobTargetId to the target optional ID, even if the schema is not Blob-bearing. None versus Some or different strings is InvalidInput before lease/compatibility/options checks. It does not validate Dataset/base authority from the opaque ID.

Clone every supplied lease together with original part index, sort by range start, and reject adjacent overlap when right.start<left.end, reporting both original indices/ranges. Touching endpoints are legal. This compares whole declared leases, even if no managed values used them or inputs are non-Blob; no per-value ID set is computed. None leases do not participate.

Build PreparedInput borrowing cached part metadata and normalized part schema, then concat_prepared allows Blob columns and disables reuse. No input metadata refresh or Blob revalidation occurs at assembly. DataFilePart::open is the capability boundary, while input immutability and target storage identity remain caller obligations.

Private cfg(test) module imports local ObjectStore,scheduler,CachedFileSize,temp paths,Atomics and AsyncWriteExt. write_file makes one Int32 value root from supplied i32 values, constructs a current exact writer with default options, writes once,finishes and returns schema. All fallible operations unwrap; helper is not a historical fixture generator.

input helper creates a testing ScanScheduler, opens the path with unknown size and attaches caller expected rows. The helper itself never compares the row count; only concat/open validation uses that option.

V2_1 concat success writes input values[1,2,3] and[4,5]. Atomic factory must run once; result must be Written with5rows; reopened metadata must report5rows,two pages and strictly increasing page priority. No payload RecordBatch is read, no exact offsets/sizes or byte equality are asserted despite the test name mentioning relocated metadata.

Same test concatenates the first input alone, supplies an error-returning counted factory, and requires Reused(0,_) plus zero calls. It does not assert reused output version/rows/size or compare input bytes.

Schema-metadata rstest runs V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3. Each fixture writes two identical[1,2] batches in separate files with schema key review-key=review-value. Defaults select all other writer policies; no nested type or Blob fixture.

Concat both metadata-tagged inputs and require Written. Reopen output metadata and assert schema key preserved. Expected4rows is merely stored in helper input then bypassed by direct read_all_metadata; no row-count assertion or decoded-value equality exists here.

Mixed-version test suppliesV2_1 thenV2_2 againstV2_1 target. Require Unsupported VersionMismatch at input1 and factory count0. Wildcard does not assert exact actual/expected fields and does not test target/schema/column incompatibility combinations.

Legacy test obtains target schema from a newly writtenV2_1 file, copies checked-in exact_versions/v1.lance bytes to a local object and shuts it down. It supplies expected rows0 for the legacy input, yet requires Unsupported LegacyVersion and factory0, illustrating legacy precedence before expected-row comparison. All six binary fixture contents are now fully interpreted in dedicated supplements.

White-box compatibility test loads a2rowV2_1 input and replaces its first ColumnInfo with one column-level buffer(0,1). Direct check_compatibility must return ColumnBuffers(input0,column0,count1). No serialized malformed file or output factory is involved.

Same white-box test clears normalized column_infos while preserving schema/footer, calls compatibility and asserts CorruptFile plus schema requires1physical columns substring. This tests external metadata validation before baseline column-count reasoning.

Same test clones normalized pages, decrements first num_rows by1 and rebuilds ColumnInfo. check_compatibility must return CorruptFile containing descriptor reports2physical rows. It mutates only in-memory normalized metadata, not file protobuf bytes, and does not exercise copy_page_buffers.

Overlap test uses ordinary Int32 non-BlobV2_1 files opened as DataFilePart with declared leases1..10 and5..20 and targetIDNone. Open accepts unused leases; both valid row expectations are1. No managed Blob descriptors or payloads are created.

Part concat overlap must produce an error naming both part0range1..10 and part1range5..20, and factory count remains0. Error variant is not asserted. This proves whole-declared-range overlap rejection even without Blob columns; not Blob-ID content validation.

Missing-input test writes valid and soon-deleted2rowV2_1 files, opens scheduler before deleting the latter, then concatenates both. Requires only is_err and factory0; no error type/message or missing-source recovery assertion.

Corrupt-input test writes literal not a Lance file, shuts down and concatenates with a valid input. It asserts only is_err. Its factory itself returns Err and has no call counter, so this oracle alone does not prove the factory was never called. File ends with seven tests(one four-version matrix) and two helpers. No local decoded-payload equality, Blob descriptor/null/container, zero-threshold, single-part-write, short/extra IO, abort/cancellation or overflow tests.

files.role: Public V1 value-decoding dispatch and persisted schema dictionary write/load helpers. Concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are child modules; this facade separates frozen V1 grammar from version-free IO and modern encodings.
files.limits: All physical lines of this file were read during ANALYZE60. Tests were inspected, not executed. Source remains read-only and offline; no build, test, benchmark, fixture generation or dependency installation was run. Frozen V1 behavior is recorded for compatibility, not proposed as the basis for new features. Concrete V1 binary/plain/dictionary codecs are now analyzed; full V1 reader is now analyzed; V1 statistics are fully analyzed; narrow external caller/helper context is recorded separately. Arithmetic, malformed-input, allocation and cancellation consequences are source-level observations, not executed reproductions. No unsafe block or global mutable state is declared in this file.
ranges: SPDX and module contract place V1 wire layout and schema dictionary payloads in this versioned module. Public binary,dictionary,plain children; Arrow arrays/types/DataType, async_recursion, local DataTypeExt, core schema/errors, Reader/Writer and ReadBatchParams dependencies. Only binary/plain concrete codecs are used by these dictionary-value helpers; dictionary child handles keys elsewhere.

read_binary_array is public async with borrowed Reader/DataType, nullable, byte position, logical length and generic Into<ReadBatchParams>. It converts params first, then Utf8 instantiates BinaryDecoder<Utf8Type> and awaits get. Offset/range/null/layout validation and IO are delegated to the concrete decoder, not added here.

Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary dispatch to their corresponding Arrow generic BinaryDecoder. Any other type gives InvalidInput with displayed data_type. This exact four-type set is narrower than local DataTypeExt::is_binary_like, which also includes Utf8View/BinaryView; therefore passing the broad binary-like predicate does not guarantee successful dispatch.

read_fixed_stride_array first checks DataTypeExt::is_fixed_stride and returns Schema error with type if false. It invokes PlainDecoder::new before params.into; the concrete constructor is now known to return Ok unconditionally (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:211-224). It has no nullable argument or local bounds check. Fixed-list range reads recurse, but FixedSizeList<Boolean> take reaches byte_width without a Boolean width (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:252-279; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:379-391; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182).

write_schema_dictionaries mutably borrows writer and schema. It computes maximum field ID once, defaults to-1, then iterates every integer0..=max, looks up a mutable field and skips holes or nondictionary types. Runtime work depends on ID span, not only field count; negative-only/empty schemas iterate nothing. Field data_type conversion uses the core schema contract and may panic for malformed logical metadata.

For a dictionary field, absent dictionary metadata is IO error naming field; absent in-memory values is InvalidInput naming field. Existing dictionary values are borrowed, not removed. Checks occur per field during traversal, so a later field failure does not undo earlier writes or schema mutations.

Choose encoder using actual values.data_type(): is_numeric -> PlainEncoder, otherwise is_binary_like -> BinaryEncoder, otherwise Schema error. Await encode on a one-array slice; after success store returned position and values.len in dictionary offset/length. No local comparison to schema dictionary value type, flush/shutdown, rollback or all-fields preflight. Numeric write predicate is not the explicit eight-integer read whitelist; broad binary-like predicate includes views that read_binary_array rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types as InvalidInput, while PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers through byte_width (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115). Full V1 reader is now analyzed; V1 writer lifecycle is now analyzed; statistics algorithms are now analyzed; backend lifecycle remains pending.

Private async_recursion populate_field_dictionary branches on schema-declared DataType::Dictionary, requires metadata(IO error), and for binary-like values calls read_binary_array(nullable=true,stored offset/length,full range). Existing in-memory values do not bypass this load. IO can occur before later fields fail; helper holds mutable field state across await.

Only Int8/16/32/64 and UInt8/16/32/64 dictionary value types enter fixed-stride loading with full range. Other nonbinary types produce Schema error with value_type, even though writer selection uses the broader numeric predicate. Binary view types enter the preceding branch but fail the four-type binary dispatcher as InvalidInput. No type fallback/migration is implemented.

After successful load replace dict_info.values with Some(array). A dictionary node does not recurse into children; nondictionary nodes recursively process children in stored order. Error stops traversal after any prior successful mutations. async_recursion boxes recursive futures; no task is explicitly spawned, and no rollback or cancellation guard appears.

populate_schema_dictionaries is public async, processes roots sequentially through the recursive helper, then returns unit. Empty schemas succeed without reads. File ends without tests, so local dictionary type asymmetry, invalid IDs, partial failure and view behavior have no unit oracles here; other modules must be checked separately.

ranges: SPDX/imports: BTreeMap makes grouped batch IDs ordered; Range describes half-open selections; file Fields/FieldsWithMeta and shared pb convert flat schemas; core Schema, DeepSizeOf and errors plus IO ProtoStruct provide metadata integration.

Metadata derives Debug,Default,DeepSizeOf,PartialEq; public fields batch_offsets:Vec<i32>,page_table_position:usize,manifest_position:Option<usize>,stats_metadata:Option<StatisticsMetadata>. Defaults are empty/0/None/None. ProtoStruct associates pb::Metadata. The type imposes no nonnegative/monotone offsets or valid file-position invariant at construction.

From<&Metadata> for pb::Metadata clones offsets and optional statistics leaf IDs, flattens stats schema via FieldsWithMeta but persists only fields, casts positions to u64, and maps absent manifest_position to0. Statistics Some(empty schema) remains Some; None remains None. Schema-level metadata is omitted from this stats encoding. No IO or validation.

TryFrom<pb::Metadata> clones incoming batch_offsets despite owning message, casts all positions to usize without checked conversion and always produces Some(manifest_position), including Some(0). Statistics schema is reconstructed with empty schema-level metadata and can fail through Schema conversion; IDs/position are copied without checks. Thus Metadata None manifest location roundtrips as Some(0), while wire0 retains its external-manifest sentinel meaning for consumers. Offset order/count and page ranges are not validated here.
BatchOffsets is public Debug/PartialEq with batch_id:i32 and offsets:Vec<u32>. Values describe one batch and in-batch row offsets; there is no constructor validation or ownership-sharing wrapper.

num_batches returns0 for an empty offsets vector, otherwise len-1. len returns final signed offset cast to usize, default0; negative final values become large unsigned lengths. is_empty compares that result to0. These methods assume a cumulative sentinel vector; a singleton nonzero vector reports0batches but nonzero length.

push_batch_length inserts initial0 only if offsets is empty, then appends ordinary i32 sum of supplied length and last offset. Zero or negative lengths are accepted; overflow is not checked. Existing malformed offset vectors are not repaired. Nonempty guarantee makes the last unwrap structurally safe after initialization.

get_offset casts signed batch_id to usize and uses bounds-checked Vec::get. get_batch_length first gets offset(batch_id+1), then subtracts offset(batch_id) or default0. IDs are not explicitly validated: for batch_id=-1, next0 may yield the first offset while current negative lookup misses. Signed increment/subtraction are unchecked. Terminal sentinel is accessible by get_offset even though it is not a batch start.

group_indices_to_batches documents sorted input but actually clones and sort_unstable sorts it. It scans increasing batch_id across cumulative ends and groups original absolute indices into an ordered BTreeMap, preserving duplicate values. Out-of-range IDs can advance to batch_id==num_batches and are retained there; no error is returned. A zero-length batch is skipped while its end<=index. Sorting changes caller ordering without a permutation result. The comment labels sort_unstable quick sort; that implementation claim is only a comment, not established by this file.

Map iteration yields increasing batch IDs. Each group reads batch_offsets[batch_id] and subtracts that offset cast to u32, collecting BatchOffsets. Nonempty indices with entirely empty batch_offsets panic on this indexing; a nonempty sentinel vector permits a terminal pseudo-batch for out-of-file rows. Unsigned subtraction is unchecked on malformed offsets. An empty indices slice yields no groups. The observed V1 take consumer rejects batch_id>=num_batches later.

range_to_batches returns Result but first unwraps final offset, so empty metadata panics. Only range.end>last_as_usize is explicitly rejected as InvalidInput with range/bound. It casts start to i32 and binary-searches offsets, using insertion_point-1 on a miss. Unsorted/nonzero-first offsets, large casts and underflow are not checked; duplicate cumulative offsets permit binary_search to select any matching entry. It does not reject start>end.

Iterate from chosen batch while below num_batches; stop once batch_start>=range.end. Append clamped(relative start..end) using unchecked usize subtraction, then return vector. Reversed ranges can yield reversed subranges; an empty range inside a nonempty batch can produce an empty subrange, while an empty range at its start stops immediately. The V1 reader short-circuits Range::is_empty before invoking this helper, so these helper-level observations are not claims that that caller exposes them.

StatisticsMetadata derives Debug,PartialEq,DeepSizeOf and exposes schema:Schema,leaf_field_ids:Vec<i32>,page_table_position:usize. Documentation describes per-field i.null_count/min_value/max_value names; this container does not enforce those names, schema/ID cardinality or statistics completeness.

Private cfg(test) module imports parent. test_group_indices_to_batch pushes20twice, groups[6,24], requires two groups exactly(batch0,[6])and(batch1,[4]). It does not test sorting, duplicates, empty metadata, boundaries, invalid indices, negative offsets or conversion presence.

test_range_to_batches builds lengths[5,10,15,20], cumulative[0,5,15,30,50]. Asserts0..10->[0:0..5,1:0..5],2..10->[0:2..5,1:0..5],15..33->[2:0..15,3:0..3],14..33->[1:9..10,2:0..15,3:0..3]. No error, empty/reversed range, duplicate-offset or overflow oracle. File ends with two tests; protobuf/schema conversion has no direct unit roundtrip here.

ranges: SPDX and module documentation identify the canonical V1 reader/writer/metadata/page-table home, historical accepted footer identities(0,0..=2) and emitted(0,2). Those numbers are a declared contract here; exact version parsing/constants and writer call sites are elsewhere. Five child modules are public. BTreeMap, Arc, core Field/Schema/Result and shared ReaderProjection are the local dependencies.

Private append_field_ids walks supplied fields preorder. Cast each signed field.id to u32, append a mapped column if present, silently skip an unmapped node, then recurse into children unless the node is Blob or packed struct. A missing parent does not block ordinary children. Supplied map values are neither bounds-checked nor deduplicated; negative IDs wrap to u32. Blob/packed descendants never contribute separately.

Public projection_from_field_ids allocates an index vector, uses the above traversal, and clones the supplied Schema into a fresh Arc. This follows the derived Clone implementations of Schema, Field and Dictionary; loaded dictionary ArrayRef members retain shared array storage, so this is not a promise to copy all backing data (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:24-31; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-161; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:561-568). It returns ReaderProjection directly, even for empty schema/indices, absent mappings or repeated physical values. It preserves the full supplied schema rather than removing unmapped fields; validation is a consumer responsibility. No IO or fallible Result.

projection_from_whole_schema builds the private full-schema ID-to-column map, then applies the same projection helper. Map creation uses two temporary vectors and a BTreeMap; duplicated field IDs collapse to the last assigned column in the map and may be repeated again in traversal. This is not a one-to-one mapping validator.

projection_from_column_names builds physical mapping from the original full schema before calling Schema::project. Projection errors propagate; otherwise compute indices from projected preorder using original physical columns. It does not renumber the selected subset or validate uniqueness/bounds beyond delegated schema projection.

physical_column_count returns1 for any Blob or packed struct without visiting descendants; otherwise returns1 plus recursive child counts. Ordinary struct/container parents count even when they have no data page. Addition/sum are unchecked usize arithmetic; recursive depth is not bounded.

data_file_columns creates parallel Vec<i32> IDs/indices and calls private preorder appender with a temporary counter0. Empty schema yields two empty vectors. Field IDs remain their original signed values, while physical indices are assigned consecutively.

Private field_id_to_column_index zips the parallel vectors, casts both sides to u32 and collects BTreeMap. Duplicate IDs overwrite earlier entries; negative IDs/overflowed signed columns are not rejected. The map is only a projection helper, not persisted itself here.

append_physical_fields emits every visited node ID and current physical counter before ordinary i32 increment and recursive descent. Blob/packed struct stop recursion; other parent/child nodes each occupy a slot. No overflow, duplicate-ID, negative-ID or schema validation. File ends without a local test module; compatibility/projection tests in other analyzed files do not constitute exhaustive edge-case coverage of these helpers.

ranges: SPDX/imports bring Arrow Int64 builder/array/DataType, core DeepSizeOf/errors, BTreeMap, Tokio AsyncWriteExt, Reader/Writer and V1 PlainDecoder. This writer emits an Arrow values buffer directly, while loader delegates array decoding to the concrete PlainDecoder.

PageInfo is public Clone/Debug/PartialEq/DeepSizeOf with position:usize and length:usize. new stores both without validation. Observed fixed/binary/dictionary writer callers pass logical array length, not encoded byte size; length interpretation belongs to the page encoding.

PageTable is public Debug/Default/Clone/PartialEq/DeepSizeOf; private pages maps signed field_id -> signed batch_id -> PageInfo in sorted BTreeMaps. Default is empty. Clone duplicates maps and values; no Arc/cache or interior mutation is owned here.

Public async load accepts borrowed reader, table position, signed inclusive min/max IDs and signed number of batches. Documentation requires caller dimensions and explains0/0 for absent/struct pages. Only max<min is explicitly rejected, as Internal with both values; negative IDs or num_batches are not rejected.

Count inclusive field-ID range, compute ordinary usize length=num_columns*(num_batches as usize)*2, construct Int64 PlainDecoder and await decode, then unwrap Int64 downcast. Multiplication/casts, decoded length and values are not independently checked here. Negative batch count can imply a huge requested length; concrete IO/decode failures are delegated. Whole raw table is decoded before map expansion.

For every field in the inclusive range insert an inner map; for batch0..num_batches use signed idx=field_pos_as_i32*num_batches+batch and read pair at2idx,2idx+1. Convert each signed64 position/length to usize unchecked and insert, including0/0 holes. Map lookup unwrap follows local insertion; array indexing relies on decoded shape. Negative values are not rejected. num_batches0 returns nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps, a state the writer does not safely handle.

write documents dense placeholders. Reject completely empty outer map with InvalidInput source empty page table. Then reject supplied min_field_id>observed minimum with InvalidInput whose message uses field_id_offset. Take observed max and build inclusive[min,max]. Lower min is allowed to include ancestor/hole fields; all checks here precede writer.tell.

Await writer.tell for start position, then find maximum batch key across all inner maps, unwrap it, and add1. Nonempty outer/all-empty inner maps panic at unwrap after tell; batch-ID max overflow and casts are unchecked. Int64Builder capacity is field_count*num_batches, although two values will be appended per cell, so it underestimates final element count. No dimensions are persisted in this method.

Iterate field-major then batch0..num_batches. Existing PageInfo appends position and length cast to i64; missing pair appends[0,0]. Finish Int64Array and write_all its first Arrow buffer directly, then return prior tell position. No explicit endian conversion, alignment, length prefix, footer, flush/shutdown or atomic/abort guard appears. A partial write/error/cancellation can leave output bytes; successful return is not publication/durability. A table whose only batch key is-1 derives0batches and writes an empty buffer; more negative/overflowed dimensions remain unchecked.

set inserts/creates field map and overwrites an existing same(field,batch) entry, discarding the old value. Accepts negative field/batch IDs and arbitrary PageInfo. Struct/hole zero entries are not automatically added in memory.

get returns borrowed Option<&PageInfo> via two map lookups. A missing entry is None; an explicit or loaded0/0 entry is Some, so sparse pre-write and dense post-load maps need not compare equal. No IO or normalization.

Private cfg(test) module imports temp file, pretty equality and LocalObjectReader. test_set_page_info creates PageInfo(1,2), stores at(10,20), unwraps get and compares. No overwrite/missing/negative-key tests.

Roundtrip fixture sets populated cells(10,2),(11,1),(13,0..3) to(1,2), leaves field12 absent, supplies leading struct field9, writes to local tempfile, explicitly shuts down, then loads fields9..13 with4batches. Read/write success is unwrapped; fixture spans20cells.

Test expected is actual.clone(), not original sparse fixture. It overwrites14 known missing cells with(0,0), then compares expected==actual. Therefore it verifies those holes/ancestor rows were decoded as zeros, but does not independently assert the six populated cells retain(1,2), table byte length/order or all expected shape. The test name alone does not establish full roundtrip correctness.

Error test first requires empty write error to be InvalidInput with empty-page substring, then inserts(0,0)->(1,2) and requires write(min1) InvalidInput with exact offset/min substring. Files are recreated/truncated between calls; no read/write failure injection or offset-state assertions.

Error test writes valid min0 table, opens reader without explicit shutdown of this last writer, calls load(min1,max0,batches1) and asserts Internal/message before any decoding. No reversed batch count, zero-batch rewrite, signed-size, overflow, corrupt table or partial IO test. File ends with three tests.
